questions.text: A user enters =VLOOKUP(E2,A2:C50,3,TRUE) on an unsorted product list and gets wrong prices for some codes. Which change will make the function return only exact matches?
questions.explanation: The fourth argument controls the match: TRUE (approximate) needs sorted data, FALSE gives an exact match.
steps: Spot what the question tests: VLOOKUP: range_lookup argument.
Option B (Replace 3 with 2) is out: It changes the returned column, not the matching mode.
Option C (Replace A2:C50 with C2:C50) is out: The lookup column must remain the first column of the range.
Option D (Replace VLOOKUP with HLOOKUP) is out: HLOOKUP searches across rows, not down a column.
Common slip to avoid: Believing that the column number controls accuracy.
So the answer is option A: Replace TRUE with FALSE.
questions.trap: Believing that the column number controls accuracy.
wrongReasons: It changes the returned column, not the matching mode
The lookup column must remain the first column of the range
HLOOKUP searches across rows, not down a column

questions.text: While editing a formula in Excel, which key is pressed to cycle a cell reference between relative, absolute and mixed forms such as $A$1 and A$1?
questions.explanation: F4 toggles the dollar signs in a reference being edited.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Absolute, relative and mixed references.
Option A (F2) is out: It puts the cell in edit mode.
Option C (F9) is out: It recalculates formulas.
Option D (F5) is out: It opens the Go To dialog.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing F2, which starts editing.
So the answer is option B: F4.
wrongReasons: It puts the cell in edit mode
It recalculates formulas
It opens the Go To dialog

questions.text: Which Excel tool summarises a large table by letting the user drag fields into rows, columns and values areas?
questions.explanation: A PivotTable aggregates and cross-tabulates data without altering the source.
steps: Spot what the question tests: PivotTable, Goal Seek, Scenario Manager.
Option A (Goal Seek) is out: It finds the input needed to reach a target result.
Option B (Scenario Manager) is out: It stores sets of input values.
Option D (Data Validation) is out: It restricts the values that can be entered.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Goal Seek because it is also a what-if tool.
So the answer is option C: PivotTable.
questions.trap: Choosing Goal Seek because it is also a what-if tool.
wrongReasons: It finds the input needed to reach a target result
It stores sets of input values
It restricts the values that can be entered

questions.text: A school wants to send the same letter to 300 parents, each addressed by name from an Excel list. Which Word feature should be used?
questions.explanation: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source to produce personalised copies.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Mail Merge.
Option A (Macro) is out: It records and plays a series of actions.
Option C (Cross-reference) is out: It links to another part of the document.
Option D (Template) is out: It stores a layout but not a data source.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Template, which has no data link.
So the answer is option B: Mail Merge.
questions.trap: Choosing Template, which has no data link.
wrongReasons: It records and plays a series of actions
It links to another part of the document
It stores a layout but not a data source

questions.text: In a Word report, the front pages should be numbered i, ii, iii and the main chapters should restart at 1. Which of the following is essential?
options: Insert a page break between the two parts
Apply the Heading 1 style to the first chapter
Insert a Next Page section break and unlink the footer of the new section
questions.explanation: Different number formats need separate sections and a footer that is not linked to the previous one.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Sections, headers and footers.
Option A (Insert a page break between the two parts) is out: A page break does not create a separate numbering scheme.
Option B (Apply the Heading 1 style to the first chapter) is out: Styles do not control page-number formats.
Option D (Use Print Layout view) is out: The view does not alter numbering.
Common slip to avoid: Using a simple page break.
So the answer is option C: Insert a Next Page section break and unlink the footer of the new sec….
wrongReasons: A page break does not create a separate numbering scheme
Styles do not control page-number formats
The view does not alter numbering

questions.text: In PowerPoint, which option controls how one slide changes to the next in a slide show?
questions.explanation: Transitions are applied between slides; animations act on objects inside a slide.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Transition vs Animation.
Option A (Animation) is out: It controls the movement of objects within a slide.
Option C (Slide Master) is out: It defines the layout of all slides.
Option D (Hyperlink) is out: It links to another location.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Animation.
So the answer is option B: Transition.
wrongReasons: It controls the movement of objects within a slide
It defines the layout of all slides
It links to another location

questions.text: Which key combination opens Task Manager directly in Windows?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager without the security screen.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Windows shortcuts.
Option A (Ctrl + Alt + Tab) is out: It keeps the task switcher open.
Option B (Alt + Shift + Esc) is out: It cycles through windows.
Option D (Windows + Tab) is out: It opens Task View.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing it with Ctrl + Alt + Delete.

questions.trap: Mixing it with Ctrl + Alt + Delete.

It opens Task View

questions.text: An attacker corrupts DNS data so that users typing the correct bank address are sent to a fake site. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: Pharming redirects users to fake sites even when the address is typed correctly.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Phishing vs pharming.
Option A (Phishing) is out: It lures users by messages, not by changing DNS.
Option C (Spoofing a MAC address) is out: It acts on the local network.
Option D (Keylogging) is out: It records keystrokes on a device.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing phishing because both lead to fake sites.
So the answer is option B: Pharming.
questions.trap: Choosing phishing because both lead to fake sites.
wrongReasons: It lures users by messages, not by changing DNS

questions.text: Malware that encrypts the files of a user and demands payment for the key to decrypt them is called:
questions.explanation: Ransomware locks data and demands a ransom.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of malware.
Option A (Spyware) is out: It secretly collects information.
Option B (Adware) is out: It displays advertisements.
Option D (Rootkit) is out: It hides the presence of other malware.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing it with spyware.
So the answer is option C: Ransomware.
wrongReasons: It secretly collects information
It displays advertisements
It hides the presence of other malware

questions.text: Which property makes a cryptographic hash function such as SHA-256 useful for checking the integrity of a downloaded file?
options: The digest can be reversed to recover the file
The digest length grows with the file size
The same digest is produced for any two files
A small change in the file produces a completely different fixed-length digest
questions.explanation: Any change in the input alters the digest unpredictably, so tampering is noticed.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Hash functions and integrity.
Option A (The digest can be reversed to recover the file) is out: Hash functions are one-way.
Option B (The digest length grows with the file size) is out: The output length is fixed.
Option C (The same digest is produced for any two files) is out: This would be a collision and defeats the purpose.
Common slip to avoid: Thinking a hash can be decrypted.
So the answer is option D: A small change in the file produces a completely different fixed-leng….
questions.trap: Thinking a hash can be decrypted.
wrongReasons: Hash functions are one-way
The output length is fixed
This would be a collision and defeats the purpose

questions.text: In a modern processor, which memory is the fastest and the smallest?
questions.explanation: L1 cache sits closest to the core and has the shortest access time.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Memory hierarchy.
Option A (L2 cache) is out: Larger and slower than L1.
Option B (Main memory (RAM)) is out: Much larger and slower.
Option D (Secondary storage) is out: Largest and slowest.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing RAM because it is called main memory.
So the answer is option C: L1 cache.
questions.trap: Choosing RAM because it is called main memory.
wrongReasons: Larger and slower than L1
Much larger and slower
Largest and slowest

questions.text: Which type of ROM can be erased by exposing the chip to ultraviolet light and then reprogrammed?
questions.explanation: EPROM has a quartz window for UV erasure; EEPROM is erased electrically.
steps: Spot what the question tests: PROM, EPROM, EEPROM.
Option A (PROM) is out: It can be programmed only once.
Option B (EEPROM) is out: It is erased electrically.
Option C (Mask ROM) is out: It is programmed at the factory.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing EEPROM.
So the answer is option D: EPROM.
wrongReasons: It can be programmed only once
It is erased electrically
It is programmed at the factory

questions.text: What is the binary representation of the decimal number 45?
steps: Spot what the question tests: Decimal to binary conversion.
Option B (101011) is out: Equals 43.
Option C (110101) is out: Equals 53.
Option D (100111) is out: Equals 39.
Common slip to avoid: Misplacing one of the bits.
So the answer is option A: 101101.
wrongReasons: Equals 43
Equals 53
Equals 39

questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, written in hexadecimal groups.

Option A (32) is out: This is IPv4.
Option B (64) is out: Only half of an IPv6 address.
Option C (256) is out: Twice the actual size.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the IPv4 size.

questions.text: Which protocol is connectionless and is typically used for live video streaming where speed matters more than guaranteed delivery?
questions.explanation: UDP sends datagrams without handshakes or retransmission.
steps: Spot what the question tests: TCP vs UDP.
Option A (TCP) is out: It is connection-oriented with retransmission.
Option C (FTP) is out: It transfers files over TCP.
Option D (SMTP) is out: It sends email over TCP.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing TCP because it is 'more reliable'.
So the answer is option B: UDP.
questions.trap: Choosing TCP because it is 'more reliable'.

questions.text: Which default port number is used by HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS runs on port 443 by default.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Common port numbers.
Option B (80) is out: The default port of HTTP.
Option C (21) is out: The control port of FTP.
Option D (25) is out: The default port of SMTP.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing 80.
So the answer is option A: 443.
wrongReasons: The default port of HTTP

questions.text: A software team wants to deploy its application without managing servers, operating systems or runtime installation. Which service model suits this?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides the runtime and platform, leaving the developer to manage code and data.
steps: Spot what the question tests: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS.
Option B (Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)) is out: The team must manage the operating system and runtime.
Option C (Software as a Service (SaaS)) is out: It delivers a finished application, not a place to deploy one.
Option D (Network as a Service) is out: It is not the standard fit.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing IaaS or SaaS.
So the answer is option A: Platform as a Service (PaaS).
wrongReasons: The team must manage the operating system and runtime
It delivers a finished application, not a place to deploy one

questions.text: Which software layer allows several virtual machines to share a single physical server?
questions.explanation: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Virtualisation and hypervisor.
Option A (Compiler) is out: It converts source code to machine code.
Option B (Firewall) is out: It filters network traffic.
Option C (BIOS) is out: It starts the computer.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing BIOS.

It filters network traffic

questions.text: Which SQL command removes all the rows of a table but keeps the table structure for future use, and is usually not logged row by row?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE empties the table quickly while keeping its definition.
steps: Spot what the question tests: DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP.
Option B (DROP) is out: It removes the table structure as well.
Option C (DELETE without WHERE) is out: It removes rows but logs each row and can be rolled back.
Option D (ALTER) is out: It changes the structure of the table.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing DROP.
So the answer is option A: TRUNCATE.
wrongReasons: It removes the table structure as well
It removes rows but logs each row and can be rolled back
It changes the structure of the table

questions.text: In a relational database, which key in one table refers to the primary key of another table and enforces referential integrity?
questions.explanation: A foreign key links tables and ensures that references exist.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of keys.
Option A (Candidate key) is out: It is a possible primary key.
Option B (Super key) is out: It uniquely identifies rows but may contain extra attributes.
Option C (Alternate key) is out: It is a candidate key not chosen as primary.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing it with candidate key.
So the answer is option D: Foreign key.
wrongReasons: It is a possible primary key
It uniquely identifies rows but may contain extra attributes
It is a candidate key not chosen as primary
